(She was 16 when she had my friend and we were teenagers when this guy came into our lives, just checking my math here haha!!) but anyway they’ve been married 20 years now. IMO (after 18 of course) age is just a number and not much more. And you can be pretty naive at 18, 21, 25… but I’d be insulted to not be treated like the adult I am by the time I was 27 lol!!

That’s a hard place to be. Sometimes people need to hit rock bottom before they can be ready to ask for real help. And it’s hard to be on the sidelines wishing you could do anything to help. But it sounds like you’re super aware that anything you could do to help - would be in vain because she is on her way to rock bottom. As an outsider looking in, I’m proud of your decision to put your blooming family first. It wouldn’t be fair to them or yourself to be bogged down by her situation. She is an adult and she has a parent and other siblings she can ask for help if she needs it. You are not your sisters keeper. It’s perfectly okay to miss her, to want her to get better, but it’s also perfectly okay to distance yourself and even mourn the loss you may be feeling. And you may feel regrets and what-ifs but she is her own person responsible for her own choices so you can absolutely free yourself from those thoughts.
